label: Power over a thing's esse
term: power over a thing's esse (broad power to unmake versus giving power)
resolution: Two existing definitions bind MutableThroughAnother's power relation with different readings: DEF-MUTABLE-THROUGH-ANOTHER (any other being's power to change x, the potter example) and DEF-MUTABILITY-IN-ANOTHER (the creator's power to originate or withdraw x's esse). At the respect of being they become two senses with distinct declarations. POWER_OVER_ESSE_1 (PowerOverEsse) is the broad power to make or unmake x's being, including by corruption; POWER_OVER_ESSE_2 (GivingPowerOverEsse) is the conjunction of POWER_OVER_ESSE_1 with the holder being a CAUSE_2 of x's esse; it is not a primitive giving power. The C2 batch uses POWER_OVER_ESSE_1 throughout: the power-grounding premise (PGP) and the correlation premise quantify over it, and the bridge (ii) controls use it. Under POWER_OVER_ESSE_2 the correlation premise is trivial (C2 controls, law 11) by definition of that conjunction, which does not show that a primitive creator's-power reading would trivialize it; on the conjunctive reading its content would move into the claim that every relevant power is a giving power. No argument passes from sense 1 to sense 2: the passage is exactly the correlation premise, an explicit OPEN premise, together with the can-fail-to-be disjunct.
